Today, nearly all Senate Republicans voted to advance the Clarity Act, but the motion fell short because of Senate Democrats.

We moved the ball forward, and now it’s time for the @SECGov and @CFTC to set clear rules of the road for digital assets until Congress legislates.

My focus remains on single moms and Americans living in poverty, like I did growing up. I’ll keep working to protect their hard-earned money and keep the future of finance here in America.

Growing up with a single mom in South Carolina, I learned that every dollar matters.

The Clarity Act will protect hard-earned money, keep jobs and innovation in the United States, and strengthen national security. This final text further empowers law enforcement and gives the Treasury Secretary the tools to protect community banks, farmers, and rural Americans. 

It’s time to pass the Clarity Act.

May God be near to all those forever impacted by that tragic day, and may God continue to bless this great nation.

It was great to speak with students at the College of Charleston!

Thank you, Professor Ben Navarro, for the opportunity to discuss the lessons of optimism, unity, and overcoming hardship that I’ve learned through my own experiences.

Hearing their thoughtful questions and perspectives makes me confident in the next generation of leaders South Carolina is preparing to serve our communities, state, and nation.
